roleFitSummary: You are a Developing Match for a Junior AI Engineer role (56/100). Your strongest evidence is in Flask/API development, React, JavaScript, and a completed campus-events project with SQLite, input validation, pytest tests, Git collaboration, and class presentation. The main reason to pause before applying broadly is that the role expects defensible proof of ML fundamentals, LLM application work, evaluation/monitoring, and lightweight CI or MLOps practices. Build one small, finished proof project first, then revise the resume truthfully.

resumeImprovements.text: Keep the education entry explicit: “BSc Computer Science, expected 2026.”
Place Flask/API work, React, JavaScript, Python, SQL, pytest, and Git near the top, but only where each item is already supported by the resume.
Strengthen Python and SQL evidence by connecting them to the campus-events project if accurate; for example, Python for the Flask API and SQL/SQLite for event records.
Do not list ML fundamentals, LLM development, RAG, Docker, cloud deployment, monitoring, or MLOps as skills yet. Build and document proof first.
Keep the existing collaboration and communication evidence: Git branches with two classmates and a class presentation are relevant to product-team collaboration.
Needs proof first: separate AI frameworks, deployment tools, and developer tools only after each one has visible project evidence.

roadmap.title: Week 1 — Resume review and skill review
tasks: Keep machine learning fundamentals, monitoring, MLOps, LLM development, Docker, cloud deployment, and RAG out of claimed skills until you have working evidence.
Move the supported API/backend, JavaScript, and React strengths into the top third of the resume.
Rewrite the campus-events project using only current facts: problem, implementation, technologies, and a verified result or [add verified result].

roadmap.title: Week 2 — Build proof
tasks: Build one small ML or LLM-related project with a clear user problem, expected input, expected output, and completion check.
For ML fundamentals, document the dataset, model choice, baseline, metric, and error cases.
If choosing an LLM workflow, include documented prompts, basic guardrails, a small evaluation set or checklist, and a user-facing interface.

roadmap.title: Week 3 — Validate, document, and deploy if ready
tasks: Add a README with setup instructions, how to run tests or evaluation, baseline result, one failure case, and one improvement idea.
Add a lightweight automated check that runs tests or the evaluation command, or document the manual command and expected output if automation is not yet complete.
Only add a public repository or live-demo link when it is clean, works reliably, and is easy to explain.

roadmap.title: Week 4 — Truthful resume revision and application preparation
tasks: Add the new project only after it is implemented, documented, and explainable end-to-end.
Revise skills and bullets to name only tools and methods actually used in the finished work.
Prepare interview stories about the Flask/React project, Git collaboration, class presentation, the proof project’s evaluation, and one current gap you are still addressing.
Create a working checklist for one proof project with input, output, metric, failure-case review, test/evaluation command, README, and screenshot.
Rewrite the existing campus-events project bullet without adding unsupported AI, cloud, Docker, or deployment claims.
Finish a small ML project with a dataset, model choice, baseline, metric, and documented error cases.
Add a basic evaluation note with the metric, baseline, failure cases, and one improvement idea.
Build or extend a small LLM workflow with prompts, guardrails, evaluation notes, and a user-facing demo.
Add a lightweight test or evaluation workflow and document how it is run.
Clean the repository and prepare a screenshot or short demonstration of the completed functionality.
Add cloud, Docker, RAG, or MLOps claims only after each has visible and explainable project evidence.
Reassess the resume after meaningful project completion rather than cosmetic keyword changes.
Prioritize recurring gaps across junior AI roles over collecting unrelated tools.
